faq.title: UNI International Admissions - Frequently asked questions

tuit.title: UNI International Admissions - Tuition & fees (2026-27 cost of attendance)

test_policy.notes: International first-year applicants do not need SAT or ACT; scores may be considered for scholarships (International Scholars Award can use SAT 1020+ instead of a 3.0 GPA). CDS C8 lists SAT/ACT as 'considered if submitted'; the University's Presidential Scholar award uses ACT 29+/SAT 1340+.

requirements.notes: International first-year file: application, $50 non-refundable fee, high school transcripts (unofficial accepted for admission, official required later), English test scores and financial documents. Apply with the UNI International Application or the Common App; a paper application is also accepted. Domestic application fee is $40 (CDS C13). Essay, recommendations and interview are not listed as required for international applicants.

deadlines.label: International application (fall 2027 entry): rolling
deadlines.notes: UNI admits on a rolling basis with no strict deadline for undergraduates; applying early is encouraged so a visa appointment can be secured before the semester starts. Spring 2027 and fall 2027 intakes are both mentioned on the scholarships page. The FAQ gives no decision-time promise for undergraduates.

deadlines.label: UNI Scholarship Application priority deadline
deadlines.notes: The application opens July 1 and the page prints no year; taken as Feb. 1, 2027. Applicants must be admitted first. The International Scholars Award ($2,000-$5,000/yr) needs no application.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Proof of English is required of undergraduate non-native speakers. Alternatives to a test include SAT EBRW 480+, ACT English 20+, IB English A1/A2 grade 4-7 (HL or SL), AP English Language 4-5, IGCSE/GCE A-level English grade A-C, MET 57+, Manchester Exam 400+, UNI CIEP completion certificate, or 24+ transferable semester hours from a regionally accredited U.S. college. Students without proof can be admitted conditionally and take the Culture and Intensive English Program (CIEP) on campus after a placement exam, with no separate CIEP application.

english.notes: Unrestricted (full) admission. English Pathway Program admits at TOEFL 61 (admission-policies page says 61-78): students take special credit-bearing course sections in their first semester. The 1-6 new-scale minimum is not given.
Academic overall band; IELTS Indicator also accepted. English Pathway Program: 5.5.
Certificate in C1 Advanced score of 169 or higher, for unrestricted admission.

aid.notes: Automatic International Scholars Award of $2,000-$5,000 per year (renewable up to four years) for a 3.0 GPA or SAT 1020+, no separate application. International Excel Award $1,000-$4,000 per year (needs proof of English, leadership/service examples and the UNI Scholarship Application); Presidential Scholar Award $4,000 per year (3.80+ GPA and ACT 29+/SAT 1340+, or 3.95+ GPA test-optional). Partner-state students (e.g. Taiwan, Hebei, Maharashtra) get an extra $4,000 award. CDS H6: 68 nonresident undergraduates received non-need institutional aid, average $5,771.

cost.notes: International page, undergraduate, Aug 2026-May 2027: tuition $21,578, fees $1,451, mandatory health insurance $2,520, books $500, housing and meals $10,646, personal $1,500, total $38,196. College of Business majors pay about $2,058 more as juniors/seniors.

sat.note: UNI's international pages give no SAT code; look it up in the College Board code search.

act.note: UNI's international pages give no ACT code; look it up at act.org.

toefl.note: UNI's English proficiency page gives no ETS code; select the University of Northern Iowa in the ETS list.

tier_notes.business: AACSB-accredited College of Business (UNI cites AACSB accreditation held by under 5% of business schools); regional rather than national strength.
